analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata against the indexed threats and selected TB-002/TB-011 details. scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py:73–80 introduces dev-ancestry admission restricted to RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=dev; production tag verification and current-master dispatch checks remain at 81–94. The review prerequisite gap is supported by the runbook at docs/operations/provider-release.md:542–546, rather than an imagined deployment. scripts/check-release-version.sh changes comments only; version and reported-binary checks remain equivalent. File modes are unchanged.
The runbook describes shared signing identity but separate registration credentials, namespaces and coordinator defaults (287–318, 341–436, 503–535). Official registration is not serving authorization (622–630), consistent with TB-011; no supplied change directly alters inference encryption, final authorization, billing or plaintext handling. Documented APNs sharing and model-cache/fan-helper interactions are surrounding limitations, not established new regressions.
Integration must verify release-provider.yml and release-dev-branch.yml actually enforce trusted tooling, immutable source binding and environment-scoped secrets, particularly because dev source executes after the master gate (289–294) and secrets are inherited (531–535). Reconcile these contracts with A-005/A-011/A-017 and T-054. Only metadata and a truncated orientation patch are supplied for scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh; its complete resolver behavior and callers remain unexamined. Also reconcile documented dev latest-version ordering (548–573) with publication handling before concluding availability behavior. These missing implementations are coverage limits, not proof of further vulnerabilities.

findings.detail: The new dev-push path accepts a verified commit on dev ancestry and returns without requiring reviewed master ancestry or another review check. The changed runbook explicitly states that review is not enforced on dev today and that a pull-request rule is needed before this lane runs (docs/operations/provider-release.md:542–546). Consequently, an authorized direct dev push containing unreviewed security-sensitive changes can now pass this source gate and, under the documented release chain, receive the shared Developer ID signature and dev publication. Commit-signature verification establishes provenance, not review. This weakens the reviewed-artifact prerequisite; it does not demonstrate a production registration bypass. Establish the required dev review protection before enabling the lane, or retain a fail-closed reviewed-source/approval requirement in the trusted release gate.
findings.title: Dev release source gate admits commits without the required review
